holidays.name: National Dress Up Your Pet Day
holidays.description: A day when pet owners everywhere squeeze their dogs, cats, hamsters, and even the occasional goldfish into tiny sweaters, costumes, and hats, all in the name of cuteness and social media glory.
holidays.origin: Created by pet and family lifestyle expert Colleen Paige, who founded many popular pet-focused holidays, including National Dog Day and National Cat Day.
holidays.funFact: Pet costume sales in the U.S. run into the hundreds of millions of dollars each year, and many pets are reportedly more patient about wearing hot dog costumes than their owners expect.

holidays.name: Organize Your Home Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to tackling the junk drawer, the overstuffed closet, and that mysterious box of cables nobody remembers owning. It is a perfect post-holiday reset for cluttered households.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of New Year's resolution season, popularized by holiday calendars and professional organizers encouraging people to start the year with order.
holidays.funFact: Many people discover that roughly 80 percent of the items they own are rarely or never used, which is why decluttering experts love this time of year.

holidays.name: Hot Pastrami Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A salute to the glorious stack of peppery, smoky, thinly sliced pastrami piled between slices of rye bread, ideally with mustard and a pickle on the side.
holidays.origin: A food holiday celebrating the deli classic brought to America by Romanian Jewish immigrants in the late 1800s, who adapted a traditional preserved meat called pastrama.
holidays.funFact: The word pastrami is thought to come from the Romanian word pastra, meaning to preserve, and its Yiddish-influenced spelling was shaped in New York delis.

holidays.name: Make a Drawing Day
holidays.description: A day for everyone to grab a pencil, crayon, or napkin and a pen and make a drawing, whether you're a trained artist or can barely do a stick figure.
holidays.origin: An informal creative observance listed on many holiday calendars, meant to encourage people to doodle, sketch, and loosen up their creative muscles at the start of the year.
holidays.funFact: Studies have suggested that doodling can actually help people retain information, so your meeting scribbles may be doing more good than you think.

holidays.name: Ratification Day
holidays.description: Marks the day in 1784 when the Continental Congress ratified the Treaty of Paris, officially ending the American Revolutionary War, a rare holiday that is kind of a big deal yet overlooked by most Americans.
holidays.origin: The Treaty of Paris was signed in 1783 but needed ratification by Congress, which took place in Annapolis, Maryland, on January 14, 1784.
holidays.funFact: Congress barely had enough delegates present to ratify the treaty, and the meeting was held in Annapolis because the capital was temporarily located there.
